glosses: to decelerate, to slow down
Ralentir.

examples.text: Et ce n’est pas près de décélérer puisque, aux côtés des États mentionnés plus haut, on en trouve d’autres tels que le New Hampshire et l'Idaho, qui ont récemment adopté des lois ou promulgué des règles définissant la manière dont les écoles et les collèges peuvent enseigner certaines matières.

glosses: Relever le pied sur l’accélérateur d’une automobile.

examples.text: Lors d’un changement de rapport, il est nécessaire de décélérer pour éviter l’emballement du moteur.

glosses: Diminuer la vitesse, le régime d’un moteur.

examples.text: Environ deux secondes plus tard, le moteur gauche a aussi décéléré parce qu’on avait coupé les gaz.

glosses: dafür sorgen, dass etwas die Geschwindigkeit verringert, dass es mit geringerer Geschwindigkeit vor sich geht

examples.text: Die Fahrt des Busses wurde verlangsamt.
Mit diesem Hebel verlangsamst du die Maschine.
Ich habe den ganzen Ablauf jetzt verlangsamt.

glosses: langsamer werden

examples.text: Das Tempo des Zuges verlangsamte sich.
Es ist Zeit, dass sich der Wandel in unserem Leben verlangsamt.

glosses: To reduce the velocity of something.

examples.text: In May, for example, the Illinois Central RR. introduced the long-expected streamline version of the Panama Limited, with diesel haulage, cutting the time over the 921 miles between Chicago and New Orleans by 2hr. to 18hr. each way—the fastest on record—but decelerated other trains over the same route.
The S.D.R. [Somerset & Dorset Railway] could not adhere to this schedule, and had to decelerate the service, but the original timings were restored when the M.R. and L.S.W.R. leased the S.D.R.

glosses: To reduce the rate of advancement of something, such as a disease.
To go slower.

examples.text: One of the disadvantages of increasing intermediate stops is that, as we have pointed out already, certain prestige trains have to suffer, notably the "Cornish Riviera Express", slowed 15min to Plymouth by stops at Taunton and Exeter; the "Torbay Express", decelerated 18min by stops at Reading, Westbury, Taunton and Newton Abbot; and the "Bristolian", which adds 14min in order to allow for a Bath stop and an increased load.

glosses: To decelerate.

examples.text: When approaching a bend in the road, slow down, and speed up after leaving it.
Crossing stations on single lines are laid out so that one line has a straight run through, and is signalled in each direction, avoiding the need to slow down to take the turnout into the loop.
When the long, hot journey drew to its end and the train slowed down for the last time, there was a stir in Jessamy’s carriage.
Then came the war... and everything slowed down.

glosses: To reduce the velocity, speed, or tempo of something.

examples.text: With a comfortable lead, the football team slowed down the tempo of the game.

A “moving platform” scheme[…]is more technologically ambitious than maglev trains even though it relies on conventional rails.[…]This set-up solves several problems […]. Stopping high-speed trains wastes energy and time, so why not simply slow them down enough for a moving platform to pull alongside?
The elimination of vacuum-braked wagons would be slowed down, and the Western Region's flirtation with diesel-hydraulic locomotives was questioned.

glosses: To become less intense, enthusiastic, etc., usually with a positive connotation, implying that one is stripped of exaggerated or unnecessary eagerness.

examples.text: Whoa, slow down there, bucko. Everyone will get a chance. Be patient.

glosses: To hit someone with a car or other vehicle and injure or kill them.

examples.text: He was run down while crossing the main road.

glosses: To criticize someone or an organisation, often unfairly.

examples.text: Whatever the company says, the media is going to run them down.
My sister is always running me down in front of my friends.
Don't run yourself down so much!
Ha! ha! ha! 'tis very hard for them to leave a subject they have not quite run down.

Since I have put my name in GCN and received my first paper, I have only received two letters. But the one that pissed me off […] was from Bible belt hypocrite. He sent me an envelope full of tracts about homosexuality. Well, I have this to say to whoever he is (The person that's got nothing better to do than get the GCN to see who he can run down should take a damn good look at himself).

glosses: To find something or someone after searching for a long time.

examples.text: I finally managed to run down that report. I had filed it incorrectly.

glosses: To lose power slowly. Used for a machine, battery, or other powered device.

examples.text: You need to wind up the clock every day so that it doesn't run down.
If you don't switch off the car lights, you will run the battery down.

glosses: To read quickly a list or other short text.

examples.text: Running down the list of suggestions, I can see three we can discard immediately.

glosses: To describe in the form of a rundown, a rough outline or summary.

examples.text: When the minute was up, John Jay managed to make the woman twice as nervous as he ran down the rules and the possibilities.

glosses: To reduce the size or stock levels of a business, often with a view to closure.

examples.text: The board of directors have decided to run down the stocks held in storage prior to offering the company for sale.
Social media has been full of strident criticism of a Government perceived as pursuing a conscious policy to run down - even destroy - our railway.

glosses: To decline in quality or condition.

examples.text: to run down in health

TravelWatch SouthWest Chairman Chris Irwin said: "This is intolerable. The South West deserves levelling up, not running down. SWR and its sponsors in the Department of Transport must be called to account."

glosses: To chase till the object pursued is captured or exhausted.

examples.text: to run down a stag

glosses: To run against and sink, as a vessel.

examples.text: The Jylland only missed running down a schooner by a few yards in the fog; it was a near thing—near enough, in fact, to allow of some shouted remarks between those on the bridge of the motorship and the man at the wheel of the schooner to be clearly heard.
Hiei now loomed into the action, causing the leading U.S. destroyers to scatter before the oncoming behemoth lest they be run down.

glosses: To crush; to overthrow; to overbear.

examples.text: Religion is […]run down by the prevailing licence of these times.

glosses: To approach (someone, thing or place) aggressively, as to attack.

examples.text: He ran down on Rashad and them.

glosses: To move (some copy) down to the next line.

examples.text: If they occasionally supply any additional copy after this element, run it down with a manual line break.
